column1: # The golden PDFs and documents (spec, Fixtures: PDFs: 20, including one 60-page PDF built from page pictures, one scanned
# PDF, one password-protected and one damaged; documents: one each of txt, md, rtf, docx, html and odt; and the three
# boundary PDFs of S3.10). Written by hand; kit-fixtures.sh `build golden-docs` builds the files under pdfs/ and docs/,
# `build boundary` the files under boundary/ (fixtures/golden-docs/ and fixtures/boundary/, never inside golden/).
# Tab separated, one kind of line each (the first field):
#   pdf      <path> <kind> <pages> <title> <password or ->   kind text (a text layer), picture (page pictures, no text
#                        layer), locked (a text layer, user password) or damaged (a text PDF cut after 200 bytes)
#   page     <path> <page> <text>          one line of text on that page (text kinds); {EXACT} is the query of the first
#                        exact row of fixtures/answers.csv whose file is this path
#   passage  <row id> <text>               the passage of a pdf row of the key: drawn on the row's page inside the row's
#                        box=x:y:w:h; it must hold the row's anchor= phrase (kit-fixtures.sh stops when it does not)
#   doc      <path> <text>                 a document of about 1,000 characters (the extension of the path decides the
#                        format); {ANCHOR} is the anchor= phrase of the doc row of the key for this file, {EXACT} the query
#                        of the first exact row whose file it is; \n is a line break
# Every pdfs/ path of the key (any group) has a pdf line; the locked and the damaged pdf are the two that the key does not
# name (S3.8). The key rows of the groups scanned, long60 and boundary have no line here: their text comes from the key.

column3: Field notes from the island trip. We arrived late on Tuesday and the harbour was already quiet. Marta checked the weather report twice before we unpacked anything. The reference code for the borrowed lamp is {EXACT} and it has to go back to the cabin owner. Please note that {ANCHOR}, so everyone should be at the dock by half past five. The bakery near the dock opens earlier than expected and sells warm bread. We counted four seabird nests on the cliff path and wrote down their positions in the small blue notebook. The water in the east cove was calm enough for a short swim. Next week we plan to map the footpaths between the two villages and note which signs are missing. Remember to charge the camera batteries before the long walk on Saturday. On the last evening we want to cook together in the cabin kitchen and share the leftover soup with the neighbours. The notebook stays in the green rucksack so that nobody forgets it again.

Software licences are expected to rise slightly because of the new seats. After the review in January {ANCHOR}, and the extra money is meant for two courses and one conference.
